turns.prompt_text: my Epson ES50 is not being seen by my Mac Air. This has worked in the past, the light is on, and it is receiving power. It will do that initial grasp hold of a paper; however, when I press scan, nothing occurs.
turns.response_html:
It is frustrating when a device that usually works suddenly stops communicating, especially when it clearly has power. Since your Mac is no longer "seeing" the ES-50 despite the hardware reacting to paper, the issue is likely a breakdown in the software handshake between the macOS driver and the scanner.

Here is a troubleshooting flow to get the connection back:

1. Check the Privacy Permissions

MacOS has strict security settings regarding which applications can access external devices.

  • Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security.
  • Select Files and Folders.
  • Ensure that your scanning software (like Epson Scan 2 or Image Capture) has full access permissions toggled on.

2. Reset the TWAIN Driver

The "grasping" of the paper suggests the scanner’s internal sensors are fine, but the Mac isn't sending the "Start" command.

  • Unplug the USB cable from your Mac Air.
  • Open Activity Monitor (via Spotlight/Command+Space).
  • Search for "Epson" or "Epson Scan 2". If you see any active processes, select them and click the X to Force Quit.
  • Plug the USB back in and try scanning again.

3. Use the Native macOS "Image Capture"

Sometimes the proprietary Epson software loses track of the device, but the OS can still see it.

  • Connect the scanner.
  • Open the Image Capture app (pre-installed on your Mac).
  • Look at the left sidebar under Devices.
  • If the ES-50 appears there, try to initiate a scan. If it works here, the issue is specifically with the Epson Scan 2 software, which might need a reinstall.

4. The USB-C / Hub Factor

Since you are using a Mac Air, you are likely using a USB-C to USB-A adapter or a hub.

  • Power vs. Data: The scanner can draw enough power to turn on the light and motor but may not have enough bandwidth/stability for data transfer if a hub is failing.
  • Try plugging the scanner into a different port on the Mac.
  • If you are using a multi-port hub, try a direct USB-C to Micro-B cable or a simple single-port Apple adapter if available.

5. Refresh the Print/Scan System

If the Mac has "ghosted" the device:

  • Go to System Settings > Printers & Scanners.
  • If the ES-50 is listed, right-click it and select Remove Scanner.
  • Unplug and replug the USB. The Mac should prompt you to re-add it or automatically recognize it.

Quick Hardware Check: When you press the physical "Scan" button on the ES-50, it relies on a background utility called Epson Event Manager to tell the Mac what to do. If that utility isn't running, the button will do nothing. Try clicking the Scan button within the software on your screen instead of the physical button on the device to see if that triggers the action.

Do you see any specific error messages (like "Scanner is busy" or "Scanner not found") when you open the Epson Scan 2 software?
